comments.author: @D0BR0volets
comments.text: For some reason, everyone who talks about Siberia mentions the Trans-Siberian Railway—a massive undertaking. Yet, I’ve never heard anyone mention another major railway project that spans the entirety of Siberia: the BAM (Baikal-Amur Mainline). It was even more ambitious than the Trans-Siberian Railway. While the original Trans-Siberian Railway was single-track (meaning trains could only move in one direction), the Soviet Union built the BAM as a double-track line—also stretching across all of Siberia—and subsequently upgraded the Trans-Siberian Railway by adding a second track. Please look into the BAM and create a dedicated video about it; there is very little information available on this subject in English.
